title: wg: mimi-content §5.10 defers calling out of scope; ask whether it should come in, with mimid as the report
description:
Mark, 2026-11-23: "the ietf mimi specs are pretty weak about vtc
endpoints, i cant remember if we raised emails, issues, or PRs against
the mimi IDs about it."

CHECKED THE RECORD: we have not. Nothing was raised.
- Beads: the only VTC mentions are mimid-bcji (our own binding draft,
  filed today), mimid-7yn7.5 (content coverage, which lists
  "Voice/video calls | Largely outside mimi-content; a core feature of
  every app on the list"), and two coland interop beads that mention it
  only in passing. No bead labelled `wg` about it, and nothing under
  epic mimid-1wgh.37 before this one.
- IETF notes (/data/PROJECT/IETF/notes): the only matches for `vtc` or
  `teleconference` are inside an IETF 127 **aipref** meeting transcript,
  a different working group, where the words are coincidental. No mimi
  list post, no GitHub issue, no PR.

So this is unraised, and Mark's reading that the specs are weak here
matches what the code had to invent.

WHAT MIMI GIVES US, as far as the drafts go: mimi-content has a
`session` disposition and §4.5 ExternalPart, and that is about all. The
drafts say nothing about:
- what a receiver does with a `session` part it cannot join (no scheme
  negotiation, no capability advertisement, no refusal shape);
- whether a `session` part is content to be fetched or a live endpoint
  to be dialled -- mimid decided the latter and never fetches one, but
  nothing says so;
- lifetime: whether the endpoint is still live, who ends it, whether a
  later message supersedes it. An ExternalPart has `expires`, which is
  about the URL's availability rather than a call's;
- which URL schemes are meaningful. mimid takes https and wss and puts
  anything else in the body, which is a guess;
- ringing, declining, joining, or who is already in the call -- the
  states every app on Mark's gatekeeper list has.

WHAT MIMID DID ABOUT IT, which is the evidence for a WG post: it mapped
the `session` disposition to a JMAP MessageAction of type
`urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:cap:vtc` in both directions
(project.rs:202-210, backend.rs:872-893), choosing the scheme set and
the never-fetch rule itself. That is an implementation report the WG can
use: here is what one implementation had to decide because the draft did
not.

PROPOSED, and it needs Mark's OK before anything is posted, per
AGENTS.md and the peer-contributing rules:
1. A mimi-content issue or list post asking what a receiver is expected
   to do with a `session` part, with mimid's choices as the concrete
   case. That is a question, not a proposal, and is the cheapest first
   move.
2. If the WG is interested, a draft section or a separate extension for
   call signalling. Note bead mimid-7yn7.5's observation that calls are
   "largely outside mimi-content", so this may be a separate document
   rather than a patch.
3. Either way, specify the mapping in our own
   draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00 first (bead mimid-bcji), so our
   implementation stops being ahead of its own specification.

Doing (3) before (1) is the better order: it makes the question concrete
and shows we have implemented something rather than only asking.
design:
TITLE: §5.10: what is a receiver expected to do with a session part?

BODY:
This came out of implementing §5.10 in mimid, mapping MIMI messages onto
JMAP Chat. §5.10 and the `session` disposition give enough to send a
conference invitation, and the example is clear. What a receiver should
do with one is left open, and "Further discussion of calling and
conferencing functionality is out-of-scope of this document" means that
is deliberate — so this is a question about scope rather than a defect
report.

Four things mimid had to decide with nothing to read:

- Whether a session part is rendered as a link or acted on. §5.10 offers
  both ("rendered to the user, requiring a click" or "processed
  differently by the client, for example alerting the user"), which is
  fine for a client and not enough for two implementations to agree.
  mimid acts on it: it becomes a join affordance, not body text.
- Whether a session part is content to fetch. mimid never fetches one.
  The example implies that by leaving `size`, `expires`, `encAlg` and
  `hashAlg` at 0 or none, but it is not stated, and an implementation
  that treats every ExternalPart alike would try to download the URL.
- Which URL schemes are meaningful. mimid accepts `https` and `wss` and
  puts any other scheme in the body as text. That is a guess; a SIP URI
  seems equally intended, since §1 gives interoperating with SIP as a
  goal.
- The other half of the disposition. The registry says "a description of
  a multimedia session, or URI used to join one". mimid handles only the
  URI form. For the description form there is no stated content type or
  shape, so a sender using it reaches a receiver that cannot act on it.

There is also a second half of the story in another draft, which may be
worth joining up: room-policy §5 notes that "A room can be both
fixed_membership and parent_dependent, for example, for room used for a
multi-media call of clients in a Group DM". So the room model for a call
is in room-policy, the session pointer is in mimi-content, and neither
references the other. (Separately, I think room-policy's version does not
work for the obvious case — a call with everyone in the Group DM is not a
*strict* subset of it; that is ietf-wg-mimi/mimi-room-policy#40.)

The question: should calling and conferencing come into scope somewhere?
If not, would a sentence in §5.10 on what a receiver may assume — that a
session part is an endpoint rather than content, and what to do with a
scheme or a description form it cannot use — be in scope as interop
guidance without opening up calling itself?
